variants.name: Live signal: JCI, rupiah, INDOGB 10Y trend, INDOGB–UST spread
US 10Y trend in place of the INDOGB trend
Korea-style rotation (JCI inverted: stocks down = bonds up)

ust.method: Overnight = New York closes strictly before each Jakarta close (New York shuts at about 04:00–05:00 Jakarta). Hedged = INDOGB 10Y minus β × US 10Y, β the trailing 26-week weekly beta known at the time. All variants walk-forward, z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks, thresholds ±0.5, hit rates over the next 4 weeks. The 'Beta 3Y' slot carries the INDOGB 15Y.

src: Yahoo Finance: IDX Composite (^JKSE) and USD/IDR (IDR=X) daily closes; any USD/IDR close more than 1.5% from Bank Indonesia’s JISDOR fix is replaced by JISDOR. INDOGB 10Y: PHEI IGSYC (CNBC benchmark 10Y before the first stored PHEI day). US Treasury daily par yields (2Y, 10Y; home.treasury.gov). Weekly, last trading day of each week.

method.window: 4-week changes; z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks (min 26); thresholds ±0.5
components: USD/IDR 4-week % change (inverted: a weaker rupiah is bond-bearish)
INDOGB − UST 10Y spread vs its 26-week average (wide = cheap)

method.window: 20-day changes; z-scores vs trailing 260 sessions (min 130); spread vs its 130-day average; thresholds ±0.5; hit rates over the next 20 sessions; UST hedge β = trailing 130-day daily beta
components: INDOGB − UST 10Y spread vs its 130-day average (wide = cheap)

notes.headline: The rupiah firms (JISDOR 18,059) and the JCI adds 1%, yet the daily signal slips back to −0.64 on a rupiah base effect, so the Oct 7 sell-off episode stays open; the 10Y INDOGB holds at 7.68%, 52bp higher in four weeks and mostly not explained by Treasuries. Signal −0.64: bond sell-off
notes.now: Foreign money is still out of Indonesian stocks over the month, though the selling has slowed. The JCI rose 1.02% to 5,125.73 with foreign flows roughly flat by midday (a Rp3bn net sale; who bought is not disclosed), yet it is 16.3% down over 20 sessions and 44% below its one-year peak; foreigners also sold Rp2.29tn of SBN in the first week of November, so October's bond inflows did not carry over. The rupiah firmed (JISDOR 18,059, −0.24%), but the daily signal still fell to −0.64 from −0.50, back in sell-off: the rupiah part turned bearish (z +0.61) because its 20-session window now starts at a low Sep 29 print, putting USD/IDR +1.74% over the window; the JCI part (z −1.75) and the 10Y trend part (z +1.64, the 10Y up 46.5bp over 20 sessions) also point to a sell-off, and only the spread part is bond-bullish (z +1.43), with INDOGBs paying 280bp over Treasuries, 39bp above their 130-day average and in the 96th percentile of 52 weeks; that is a nominal pick-up before currency risk. Treasuries explain little of the trend: the US 10Y fell 22bp in four weeks and the 26-week weekly beta is −0.21, so about +4.7bp of the 51.5bp four-week rise is the Treasury-linked part and +46.8bp is residual, which is what the US move does not explain rather than proof of domestic selling or political risk. On the day the link was weak again: Monday's 2bp New York sell-off implied about +0.7bp for INDOGBs at the 1-year daily beta of 0.34, yet the 10Y fell 0.4bp; INDOGBs follow large US moves in the same direction about 73% of the time, smaller ones much less reliably. The sell-off episode that began Oct 7 is still open after 17 sessions with the 10Y 51.6bp higher. On the daily build since June 2022 the signal scores a Sharpe of 0.75 outright and 0.89 hedged against Treasuries, but sell-off calls were right only 51% of the time over the next 20 sessions (rally calls 58%), and the average 10Y move after a sell-off call was −1.8bp; these are in-sample back-tests. Our read for the next 2–4 weeks: neutral on duration rather than short, because the sell-off reading leans on a base effect and the back-test gives sell-off calls little edge; the MSCI review, the Vice President's possible resignation and BI on Nov 17–18 are the risks that could turn it into a real sell-off.
notes.flip: The daily signal is in sell-off below −0.5 and sits at −0.64. A return to neutral needs a small move: roughly, the JCI holding above 5,100 while the rupiah stays near 18,050 as the late-September base rolls off the window. A deeper sell-off would come from JISDOR back above 18,200, a new JCI low below 4,900 or the 10Y above its 7.72% high. A move to bond rally (above +0.5) needs a JCI rebound and a firmer rupiah together, the pattern that started the April 2025 rally. The policy triggers are a BI-Rate hike that steadies the rupiah (bearish for the front end on the day, bullish for the trend after) or MSCI softening its Standalone proposal; a messy vice-presidential succession is the political trigger on the other side.
phases: JCI 6,500–7,250 while the 10Y rose from 6.2% to a 7.58% peak in October 2022 as global rates surged; stocks held up on the commodity boom.

JCI 6,630–7,380 and 10Y 6.19–7.21%. Stocks and bonds drifted without a clear link; on the weekly build the signal's calls lost money (Sharpe −0.3 from 2022 to August 2024), while the daily build did better over the same span.
JCI fell from 7,812 to 6,258 while the 10Y rose from 6.43% to 7.19%: stocks, rupiah and bonds sold off together, the pattern the signal is built for. Its record improves sharply from here.
JCI climbed from 6,262 to a record 9,075 on Jan 15, 2026, and the 10Y fell to 5.93% in October 2025 as foreign money returned and BI eased.

MSCI froze Indonesian index changes in January and on Oct 15 proposed Standalone status; BI hiked 100bp to 5.75% by June and now weighs more. JCI −44% from its peak to about 5,130, 10Y up to 7.68%: the second and deeper foreign exit, though foreigners still bought SBN in October. The daily signal touched −0.50 on Nov 9 and fell back to −0.64 on Nov 10, the day Vice President Gibran said he intends to resign over court rulings on his school certificate.
notes.caveats: These are proxies, not reported fund flows: daily foreign SBN holdings (DJPPR) and equity flows (IDX) are not machine-readable for the dashboard, so the rupiah and the JCI stand in for foreign money, and any statement about who bought or sold is a hypothesis. USD/IDR is Yahoo's close, replaced by Bank Indonesia's JISDOR fix on any day it strays more than 1.5% (Yahoo printed ~17,480 from Nov 3, 2026 while JISDOR was ~18,100); the 20-session windows count stored sessions, so gaps in the data stretch them. Before Oct 29, 2026 the 10Y is CNBC's benchmark-bond yield rather than PHEI's IGSYC, with repeated stale prints removed. The daily back-test runs from June 2022 (957 sessions): the live signal makes 190bp outright (Sharpe 0.75) and 220bp hedged against Treasuries (Sharpe 0.89), against −40bp for always holding the 10Y; the weekly build scores 0.42 and 0.56. Variants that use the US 10Y trend score up to 0.73 outright and 0.78 hedged on the weekly build but were picked after the fact and are not live. In-sample, no trading costs; not a trading system.
